A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same sensitivity-guided augmentation work despite different titles and substantial revision. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation experiments, corruption evaluations, component ablations, and sensitivity-analysis studies in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v5 reports original segmentation, fine-tuning, domain-adaptation, classification, ablation, and runtime results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The KID-based sensitivity estimator, equal-spacing objective, PCHIP approximation, and online augmentation framework remain. However, v1 Equations 10–11 specify accuracy-squared sampling weights within augmentation types and uniform type probabilities, whereas v5 Algorithm 1 and Section 4.6 specify accuracy-ranked Beta-Binomial sampling with parameters 0.75 and 1.0. This changes the sampling component within the retained framework.

E1.justification: v5 adds CUB bird classification in Appendix M, extending evaluation beyond segmentation, and supervised target-domain adaptation on ACDC Snow in Section 4.4, extending the previous zero-shot setting. LoveDA, evaluated in v1 Table 4, is removed. The other six segmentation datasets, ACDC, IDD, and the synthetic corruption suites remain.

E2.justification: The principal weather comparisons replace v1's generic SOTA comparator with explicitly evaluated VIPAug and IDBH methods. The diverse-dataset comparison changes from SOTA versus Ours in v1 Table 4 to TrivialAugment, IDBH, and Ours in v5 Table 3. The generic SOTA row is also removed from the retained clean-backbone comparison, now v5 Table 11.

E3.justification: The principal segmentation experiments move from PSPNet to SegFormer-b0. v1 permits early stopping and uses recommended configurations for individual baselines; v5 specifies matched configurations, fixed 160k-iteration training, and best-mIoU checkpoint selection. Reported validation and sensitivity-update schedules also change. New protocols include foundation-model fine-tuning, 20k-iteration ACDC Snow adaptation, and training-size sweeps from 1,000 to 5,000 samples.

E4.justification: v5 adds a clean-warmup ablation, training-data-size analysis, runtime/storage comparison, and dedicated windshield-wiper occlusion cases. The uniform control changes its question: v1 Table 5 removes sensitivity guidance, whereas v5 Table 6 samples uniformly among sensitivity-selected levels. Existing KID/FID, level-count, and training-curve analyses are retained in reorganized locations.

E5.justification: v5 Table 1 newly reports mean and standard deviation across four timing runs, and Section 4 states that experimental random seeds are fixed. v1 provides neither disclosure. This is a limited extension of statistical reporting: segmentation performance tables still provide point estimates without run-to-run uncertainty, and no increase in accuracy-evaluation runs is established.

E6.justification: The robustness and ablation tables contain substantially replaced results under changed experimental settings, alongside new fine-tuning, adaptation, classification, and efficiency results. Even the retained clean-backbone comparison changes entries: PSPNet RandAugment mIoU is 45.245 in v1 Table 1 and 69.360 in v5 Table 11, while Ours remains 71.840. These are reported-result changes, not evidence of same-setting performance gains across versions.

T1.justification: v5 Appendix A adds an explicit proof of the existing equal-spacing solution, establishing the bound Gmax/L and its attainability under continuity assumptions. It also clarifies the clean-data endpoint and accuracy normalization. v1 already presents the telescoping identity and equal-spacing solution, so this is a focused formalization rather than a new theoretical framework.

C1.justification: The three central contributions—adaptive sensitivity analysis, sensitivity-guided augmentation, and robustness evaluation—remain. v5 extends the advertised benefits to training-data efficiency, applicability beyond segmentation, and compatibility with foundation-model fine-tuning. Its abstract and conclusion also reduce v1's emphasis on consistently superior clean-data accuracy, while making efficiency claims more quantitative.

C2.justification: The interpretation of the revised ablations changes substantially: v1 emphasizes geometric augmentations as the dominant contributor, whereas v5 emphasizes photometric augmentations and interprets the retained channel curves as evidence of Hue sensitivity. v5 adds explanations involving extreme AdvSteer color corruption, small-object/night failures, overfitting during target-domain adaptation, and optional warmup. These replace or extend v1's explanations based on equal augmentation-type weighting and local pixel differences.

D1.justification: v5 adds a code-implementation link, a training-loop algorithm, and Table 10 detailing optimizer, learning rate, batch size, backbone variant, augmentation sets, warmup, and update intervals. Figure 13 newly specifies the sensitivity solver's 0.05 stopping threshold. These substantially improve implementation documentation beyond v1's general setup description; the linked implementation's availability was not externally verified.

R1.justification: v5 expands discussion of adversarial augmentation and segmentation-specific Superpixel-Mix, and adds references supporting VIPAug, IDBH, and foundation-model experiments. It removes the Kamann–Rother and Alomar-based motivation used in v1. The central positioning relative to AdvSteer, random augmentation, and learned augmentation policies remains.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and existing methodology exposition are substantially rewritten. The basis-augmentation background moves from the main text to Appendix J.1, the experimental narrative is reorganized, and the appendices are extensively rearranged. These changes affect the presentation of retained material as well as accommodating new experiments.

P2.justification: v5 redraws the overview diagram, adds data-size plots and occlusion examples, replaces qualitative comparisons, and restructures major tables by changing comparator rows and reducing displayed metric columns. Existing augmentation illustrations and the clean-backbone table move to the appendix, while the training sensitivity curves move into the main text. Typography and page layout also change throughout.

improvement.justification: v5 substantially strengthens empirical support by replacing loosely specified SOTA comparisons with named, more consistently controlled baselines and directly measuring the central efficiency claim in Table 1. Detailed configurations and new transfer, adaptation, and ablation experiments make the work more reproducible and its applicability better tested. These gains outweigh remaining weaknesses: the explicit no-sensitivity-analysis control is lost, accuracy uncertainty remains unreported, and some prose overstates the evidence—for example, Figure 3 does not show Ours leading at every training size, and Table 7's caption incorrectly identifies IDBH as the next-best ACDC comparator.
